label: Decide: Find in Image
description: Ask a decision model where one described thing is in an image, and get its box. Only typesafe/jev-1.14 (or ~typesafe/jev-latest) answers this question; other models refuse it. What it looks at is the ports you add, one per piece, each named and typed, at least one an Image: `product = DecisionBox(photo: Image) { provider: decider.provider, instructions: "the product in `photo`", photo: listing.photo }`. Describe the target and name the image it is in, rather than giving an order. A box always comes back, even when the thing is not there: ask a Decide: Yes or No beside it ("Is there a product in `photo`?") and use the box only when that says yes.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Which decision model and credential: wire an OpenRouter Decision Model node whose model is typesafe/jev-1.14.

inputs.name: instructions
inputs.label: Target
inputs.description: The thing to find, described, with the image it is in.

outputs.name: box
outputs.description: Its edges as fractions of the image, measured from the top-left corner: `left` and `right` of the width, `top` and `bottom` of the height.

outputs.name: confidence
outputs.description: How sure the model is of the box, from 0 to 1.

then.message: DecisionBox '{id}' takes, on each added input, exactly one of: a value made of JSON (text, a record, a dict, a list of those), a file, or a list of files, and these are none of those: {names}. Give each file a port of its own (`photo: Image`, `photos: List[Image]`) rather than a field of a record, an item of a list mixed with text, or one type with a value (`String | Image`).
DecisionBox '{id}' has nothing to decide about: add one input for each piece of what the model should judge, named after it and typed, like `DecisionBox(photo: Image)`.
